Nothing broke today, but a lot is still unresolved — which is its own kind of signal.

sections.title: World
sections.gist: Israel's election ended in deadlock, leaving Netanyahu's bloc short of the seats needed to govern alone.

items.headline: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority
items.what: Israelis voted Tuesday in an election framed as a verdict on PM Benjamin Netanyahu's 15-year rule. Wednesday's count put his right-wing bloc around **53-56 seats** — short of the **61 needed** to govern. Likud stayed the largest party, but Gadi Eisenkot's new centrist party ran a close second.
items.why_it_matters: A drawn-out coalition fight could leave Israel without a clear government for weeks, right as it manages a fragile Gaza truce and tensions with Iran.
items.context: Netanyahu has led Israel for most of the last 15 years, surviving a corruption trial and the fallout from the Hamas attacks of October 2023. No Israeli party has ever won a majority alone, so whoever leads must build a coalition from smaller parties.
items.next: Final tallies, including soldiers' and overseas votes, could take **days** and may still shift the balance of seats.
items.insight: A hung result would make Netanyahu dependent on the same far-right allies whose demands already strained his last coalition — this time with less room to maneuver.

terms.meaning: Israel's 120-seat parliament; a party or bloc needs 61 seats' support to form a government.

sections.title: Affects you
sections.gist: UPI's merchant fee is delayed again to after Diwali, and the festive trading calendar brings one extra session and one holiday.

items.headline: UPI's merchant fee delayed again, until after Diwali
items.what: The 0.4% fee on UPI payments over ₹2,000 to shops was due to start **October 15**. NPCI's steering committee postponed it on **October 13**, saying it will begin 'immediately post-Diwali' on a date still to be announced. The fee is paid by the shop, not the customer, and smaller payments stay free.
items.why_it_matters: Shops may start passing this cost on through small surcharges or by asking for cash on bigger bills.
items.context: UPI is the tap-to-pay system behind PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, free to use since 2016. Banks running it want a cut of transaction costs, so Parliament passed a law in August letting the government allow such fees.
items.next: NPCI must still name the exact start date — Diwali falls on **November 8** this year.
items.insight: Delaying twice suggests NPCI fears a consumer backlash during festive shopping, not that the fee itself is in doubt.

terms.meaning: Merchant Discount Rate — the small fee a shop pays a bank for accepting a digital payment.

items.headline: Diwali falls on a Sunday this year, Nov 8
items.what: Diwali lands on **Sunday, November 8** in 2026. Stock exchanges will run a short evening 'Muhurat' trading session that day, a symbolic tradition for the new financial year. Markets then shut again on **Tuesday, November 10**, for the Diwali-Balipratipada holiday.
items.why_it_matters: If you trade Indian stocks, mark both dates — one extra trading window, one closed session.
items.context: Muhurat trading is an hour-long session on Diwali evening where many Indian investors place a token trade for good luck. It has run every year since the 1950s, regardless of which weekday Diwali falls on.
items.next: Exact Muhurat timings, usually a short evening slot, are announced closer to the date.

sections.title: Markets & money
sections.gist: The Fed's rate call and Big Tech's earnings this week will decide how much faith markets keep in the AI spending boom.

items.headline: Fed's rate decision lands today, a hold expected
items.what: The US Federal Reserve announces its rate call today at **2pm US time** (~11:30pm IST). Traders price in roughly a **90% chance** it holds rates at 3.75%-4.00%, pausing after September's quarter-point hike. Fed chair Kevin Warsh has declined to preview the call, saying he won't 'prejudge meetings.'
items.why_it_matters: A higher-for-longer Fed keeps the dollar strong and borrowing costly worldwide, including for India's rupee and import bills.
items.context: The Fed sets the interest rate that ripples through loans, mortgages and markets worldwide. It hiked rates in September for the first time in three years, after holding them steady for months.
items.next: Most analysts now expect the next move — a possible hike — at the **December 8-9** meeting instead.
items.insight: A hold today with hawkish language would be the market's worst case: no relief now, and a hike still priced in for December.

terms.meaning: The Federal Reserve committee that meets roughly every six weeks to set the US interest rate.

items.headline: Big Tech's earnings this week test the AI spending boom
items.what: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta report quarterly earnings this week, the first real test of their AI bets. Together, the four are expected to spend over **$600 billion** on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone. Investors want proof that spending is turning into revenue, not just bigger data centers.
items.why_it_matters: A disappointing report from any of the four could trigger a broader sell-off that also hits Indian IT and tech stocks.
items.context: These four companies make up a huge share of US stock indices, so their results move the whole market. They have spent years insisting AI investment will pay off, but doubts about an 'AI bubble' have grown through 2026.
items.next: Results land through this week; watch each company's AI-spending guidance for next year, not just this quarter's profit.
items.insight: Markets have let these four run up AI spending for years on trust alone — this earnings week is where that trust gets priced.
